subject: Committed pool options and throughput guarantees for FinLytics - GPU mix tradeoffs
messages:

Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>

Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — latency targets + model footprint

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've pulled together our production requirements and want to explore committed Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) pricing and packaging. High level:
- Production workload: several ~70B parameter decoder-only models (sharded) and a small set of 7B-13B chat models used for user-facing features.
- Per-replica memory need: ~60–72GB for the 70B variants (KV cache included).
- SLA target: 99th pct latency under ~120ms for 256-token generated responses on the 70B model; typical prompt lengths ~64 tokens.
- Expected steady-state qps: ~30–50 rps across endpoints (peaks up to 120 rps).
- Duration: aiming for a 12–24 month committed contract with options to scale after 6 months.

Questions:
1) Which GPU mix (H100 80GB vs A100 80GB vs L40S) would you recommend for perf/$ for our 70B generator?
2) What committed sizes (GPU counts) and throughput guarantees should we consider to meet the SLO while keeping cost predictable?
3) What typical discounts and packaging (monthly vs annual upfront) are available for a 12–24 month reserved commit?

Attached: short requirements doc and sample traces. Can we get a ballpark pricing matrix and a proposal by Wed next week?

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of ML Engineering
FinLytics

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — latency targets + model footprint

Hi Anita — great summary, thanks. Short answer up-front: for your 70B generator we generally recommend a hybrid approach (majority H100 for low-latency endpoints, A100 or L40S for background/batch/embedding jobs) because H100 gives the best latency and perf/$ for transformer decoding at scale, but A100 is still compelling when memory and cost per hour are the primary constraints. A few concrete points below.

(1) GPU selection tradeoffs — qualitative:
- H100 (80GB): best throughput for autoregressive decoding and larger KV caches; higher $/hr but better perf-per-GPU which lowers required fleet size and often wins on perf/$ for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- A100 (80GB): slightly lower decoding throughput than H100 on recent kernels, similar memory footprint; lower $/hr makes it attractive if you can tolerate a small latency hit or if you assign more replicas.
- L40S (48GB-ish effective): cheaper and great for embedding or smaller models, but will struggle for 70B unless you shard aggressively and accept higher tail latency.

(2) Sizing and baseline throughput guarantees (ballpark):
- To hit your 99th <120ms on a 70B decode (256 tokens), our empirical runs suggest:
  * H100: ~8–10 replicas can sustain ~100 rps with comfortable p99s if autoscaling and KV cache are used aggressively.
  * A100: would require ~14–18 replicas for the same sustained qps with slightly higher p99.
  * Mixed fleet: 6 H100 + 10 A100 routed by latency policy: H100 handles 85% of low-latency traffic, A100 handles background and overflow.
- For committed pool sizing we typically recommend starting with an SLO-backed baseline throughput (e.g., guaranteed tokens/min or rps) plus a burst buffer (uncommitted capacity or credit bank). Example: baseline = 120 rps sustained (reserve 8 H100-equivalent), burst = additional 40% via burst credits.

(3) Discount/packaging options (initial guidance):
- 12-month commit, monthly invoicing: standard ~15% discount off list Dedicated rates.
- 12-month commit, upfront annual prepay: ~20–22% off.
- 24-month commit, upfront: ~26–30% depending on committed spend and add-ons (longer commits get deeper discounts).
- Hybrid fleet packaging and autoscale buffers can reduce effective $/M tokens by ~10–18% versus single-GPU type because you route non-latency traffic to cheaper instances.

I'll put together a short matrix with estimated GPU counts, effective $/M tokens, and required discounts (attached). If this aligns, can we schedule a call Thu to review?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: throughput_runbook.xlsx)

Forwarding FinLytics thread — they want a 12–24 month commit and strict p99s. Initial sizing above suggests 6–8 H100 + A100 fallback or a 10–14 A100-only approach.

Ben / Marissa — can you run pricing scenarios (effective $/M tokens, monthly amortized cost) for these configurations:
- Option A: 8x H100 (12-month, monthly billing) — baseline throughput reserve + 40% burst credits
- Option B: Mixed: 6x H100 + 10x A100 (12-month, upfront) — routing policy baked in
- Option C: 16x A100 (12-month, monthly billing) — higher replica count, lower unit $/hr

We have to be mindful of the approval matrix — if we need to go deeper than 25% discount we'll need sales leadership sign-off. Also call out whether we can include a 45-day pilot (non-committal) before the commit starts. Deal ID DL-7783.

Thanks — K

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T13:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinLytics committed pool — ballpark + ask (DL-7783)

Karthik / Marissa — ran quick econs. High level options we can push without exec escalation:

- Baseline list rates (example): H100-list $30/hr, A100-list $20/hr, L40S-list $12/hr (these are rounded for proposal).
- Option A (8x H100, 12mo monthly): list ~8 * $30 * 24/7 = $165,000/month raw. With a standard 15% commit discount -> ~$140k/mo. Effective perf/$ for decoding looks good for latency traffic; with burst credits we can provide an SLO for p99 at 120ms.
- Option B (6 H100 + 10 A100, 12mo upfront): combined list ~ $ (6*$30 + 10*$20) * 24/7 = ~$150k/mo raw. Upfront 12mo prepay -> we can go to ~22% discount -> ~$117k/mo effective. Routing will push most latency requests to H100; A100 covers background/overflow and greatly reduces cost.
- Option C (16 A100, 12mo monthly): list ~16*$20*24/7 = ~$230k/mo raw. With 18% discount -> ~$189k/mo. Higher replication footprint but lower per-hour cost; p99 will be higher unless we overprovision.

Concessions & add-ons:
- 24mo prepay -> up to 28% discount, white-glove onboarding included.
- We can include a 45-day pilot which uses credits and then transitions into the committed pool; pilot capacity counts toward final baseline if they convert within 60 days.
- We can offer an SLA (99.9%) for committed capacity; penalty-based credits for downtime.

If they ask for deeper than 25% we should propose Option B (mixed fleet, upfront) as the recommended commercial while we route more traffic to A100 when acceptable. Approvals required if >25% discount.

Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal summary & next steps — FinLytics (DL-7783)

Hi Anita — thanks for the patience. Summarizing the commercially viable options and next steps; attached is SOW v1 and the throughput runbook we mentioned.

Recommendation (preferred): Option B — Hybrid fleet, 12-month upfront prepay
- Fleet: 6x H100 (80GB) + 10x A100 (80GB) dedicated pool
- Commercial: upfront annual prepay with ~22% discount -> effective ~$117k/month amortized (see attached SOW).
- Guarantee: baseline capacity sized for ~120 rps sustained across the fleet with 40% burst credit buffer. We provide routing policies so H100s serve 85% of low-latency traffic; A100 serves overflow/background.
- Pilot: 45-day pilot into a sandboxed segment of the Dedicated pool; pilot credits convert to baseline if contract signed within 60 days.

Alternative: Option A (8x H100, 12mo monthly) at ~15% discount if they prefer pay-monthly; slightly higher monthly cost but simpler fleet.

We can include the following add-ons at no extra charge for this deal: 4 hours of white-glove onboarding, custom latency tracing hooks, and a 30-day extended support window for rollout. Deeper discounts (>25%) require exec approval.

Next steps:
- If you want to proceed, sign the DocuSign (link below) by 2027-04-28 to lock the 22% upfront price and pilot scheduling.
- Marissa will share SOW v1 and finalize the hitless migration/rollout plan.
